title: Ouray City Council Regular Meeting
location: Ouray Community Center, 320 6th Ave, Ouray, CO 81427
summary: The main business this evening is the 2027 budget. Council holds a public hearing on the proposed City of Ouray budget and takes up two ordinances on second reading: Ordinance 7 sets the 2027 rates for water, sewer, surcharge, refuse, and recycling; Ordinance 8 amends the municipal code to add a rate category specifically for light industrial operations — a new wrinkle in how the city classifies utility customers. Council also considers ratifying a Caterpillar equipment lease-purchase agreement and approving an MOU with the Ridgway Fire Protection District covering fire, EMS, training, and operational cooperation. On the liquor license side, The Yankee Girl Café has a new application before the council. The consent agenda includes four appointments to the Main Street Committee and a liquor license renewal for Ouray Lodge No. 492.

title: Norwood Water Commission Work Session
location: 1670 Naturita St, Norwood CO 81423
summary: The Norwood Water Commission sits down for a work session focused on a single item: the 2027 draft budget. Work sessions are deliberative — no formal action can be taken — so this is the commission's chance to work through the numbers before anything goes to a vote. The meeting is at Norwood Town Hall on Naturita Street at 6:00 p.m., with a Zoom option available.

title: Regular Board Meeting -- Special Meeting
location: 333 W Colorado Ave (2nd Floor), Telluride / Zoom
summary: A short special meeting — just 30 minutes on the books — with one substantive item: a proposal from Jensen Partners to provide support through the due diligence process with CommonSpirit. CommonSpirit Health is one of the largest nonprofit hospital systems in the country, and any formal due diligence engagement signals that a potential partnership, affiliation, or transaction is being evaluated seriously. The board meets at the Wellness Annex (500 W Pacific Ave) and via Zoom at 3:00 PM. The next regular board meeting is November 19.

title: Board of County Commissioners Meeting
location: 333 West Colorado Ave, 2nd floor, Telluride, CO 81435
summary: A relatively light BOCC session. The consent agenda includes acceptance of the September road report, approval of October minutes, and ratification of a letter supporting a ban on recreational prairie dog shooting on public lands. Administrative matters include a quarterly update from the Tres Rios BLM Field Office, adoption of Resolution 2027-38 setting the 2027 meeting schedule, a resolution setting the 2027 Vegetation Control and Management Fee schedule, and a professional services agreement with RMMI Digital Document Solutions to digitize Planning Department files. The Natural Resources and Climate Resilience update includes a motion to sign on to a CC4CA letter opposing legal immunity for Big Oil. The Board will also convene in executive session to discuss potential legislation related to the county's Suncor/Exxon litigation. Sitting as the Housing Authority, commissioners will consider exception requests from Esperanza Reyes to continuing residency and employment standards under her deed restriction.

title: Telluride Board of Education Work Session
location: Bridal Veil District Conference Room / Zoom
summary: The Board of Education meets Wednesday, November 4 at 3:30 PM at Bridal Veil for a work session focused on one item: interviewing student candidates for the Student Representative seat on the school board. Each candidate gets two minutes per question, covering their motivations, how they'd gather and share peer input, how they'd elevate underrepresented student voices, and how they'd manage the time commitment — which includes twice-monthly board meetings and a Colorado Association of School Boards conference in Colorado Springs, December 3–5, 2026.

location: Mountain Village, CO (see agenda for Zoom link)
summary: The Telluride Mountain Village Owners Association opens its three-meeting budget cycle for 2027 with this first session on November 6. The bulk of the afternoon goes to two substantive items: a presentation of the completed 2025 audit and tax return by CLA (Clifton, Larson, Allen LP), and a first look at the 2027 draft budget. Two more budget sessions follow — November 19 and December 3 — before the Members Meeting on December 17, where the budget is expected to be finalized. Routine minutes approval and public comment round out the agenda.
